defects.lines: behavior_notes[8] (the note "Limit: the script checks kernel functions only")
defects.before: Limit: the script checks kernel functions only. The functions that read the clock (`timed_sequence`, `timed_sequence_hot`) are listed in another file, `seq-listing.txt`. `build12.sh` says that no script uses that file [Ref6].
defects.after: Limit: the script checks kernel functions only. It does not check the code that times a kernel. The whole-chip test uses the interval mode of `bwx12` [Ref11]. In this mode the function `worker` of `bwx12.c` reads the clock, and it calls each kernel through the function `call` [Ref10]. No file in the build folder `crb-build-1` holds the machine code of `worker` or `call`. The file `seq-listing.txt` lists `timed_sequence` and `timed_sequence_hot`. These two functions read the clock in the trial mode only, and the whole-chip test does not use the trial mode [Ref10]. `build12.sh` says that no script uses `seq-listing.txt` [Ref6].
defects.evidence: In bwx12.c the only calls of timed_sequence and timed_sequence_hot are lines 2206 and 2209 inside run_trial (option --trial), the three spec files of the test hold --seq and no --trial, the clock reads of the interval mode are in worker (lines 1688 and 1700), and a grep for <worker>:, <call>: and <now_ns>: in crb-build-1/* finds nothing.

defects.before: (no entry)
defects.after: Ref10: bwx12.c, lines 90 to 94 (the two modes), 2913 and 2914 (--trial goes to trial_main), worker from line 1632 with clock reads in lines 1688 and 1700 and the kernel call through `call` in line 1695, line 1491 (`call`), lines 1995 and 2056 (timed_sequence, timed_sequence_hot), lines 2206 and 2209 (their only calls, in run_trial). Ref11: the folder of the rerun, files like.spec, cfwd.spec and crev.spec: each has --seq and no --trial, and together they name the six kernels.
defects.evidence: The corrected limit note needs citations, and the brief forbids file:line of another file inside a sentence; every cited line was read with awk and grep in this task.

defects.before: Result for that build: all 29 rows of part 1 say `same` and `ok`. All 26 rows of part 2 say `expected` and `ok`. The summary line reports 0 failed rows in both parts [Ref1].
defects.after: The output for that build is saved in the file `check_listing12.out` in the build folder `crb-build-1` [Ref1]. All 29 rows of part 1 say `same` and `ok`. All 26 rows of part 2 say `expected` and `ok`. The summary line reports 0 failed rows in both parts.
defects.evidence: The unit's extra instruction names check_listing12.out as the output, but the body text only said "the saved output" and another note says the script writes no file; the 29, 26 and 0 counts were confirmed on the file.

defects.after: New entry "Interval mode, trial mode" (same wording as the bwx12 build.txt companion). New entry "Dictionary": the Python type `dict`: a table from keys to values (same wording as the make_report companion). The register entry now ends with: A lane is one element of a vector register.

defects.before: `TARGET` is a text pattern for a branch target at the end of an instruction: ... Example: `49a4 <k_read+0x4>`. The pattern captures the address.
defects.after: Same text, plus: The page operand of an `adrp` instruction has the same form. The pattern matches it too. Example: `2f000 <__FRAME_END__+0x16a34>`.
defects.evidence: `TARGET.search("adrp x3, 2f000 <__FRAME_END__+0x16a34>")` returns the group `2f000` (tested in the scratchpad), and lines 190 to 199 of the script depend on this match to fill `page`.

defects.before: Lines 266 to 269: it must equal `want_mod`, the value of the original kernel (field `like`) in the same listing. `main` computes `want_mod` in lines 367 to 371 and line 375.
defects.after: Same text, plus: When the original kernel has no loop in the listing, `want_mod` is `None`. This is also a problem.
defects.evidence: Lines 266 and 267 of the script append the problem "... has no loop in this listing, so the loop offset cannot be compared" when `want_mod is None`, and the row had no explanation of this branch.

defects.before: ... then `add x0, x0, #0x100`, `cmp x0, x1` and a `b.cc` back to the loop start. The function has no other branch or call.
defects.after: ... and a `b.cc` back to the loop start. No instruction of the loop uses a loaded value. The function has no other branch or call.
defects.evidence: Rule 2 (line 227) requires the loop body to equal `LDP8 + 256 nop + STEP` exactly, and the `read_nop256` block of listing.txt (addresses 6cd4 to 70fc) holds only the 8 `ldp`, 256 `nop`, `add x0`, `cmp x0, x1` and `b.cc`; the brief asks to say what happens to the loaded value.

defects.before: every thread runs a sequence of kernels, and each kernel is timed in one interval.
defects.after: every thread runs a sequence of kernels, and each run of a kernel is one timed interval.
defects.evidence: The spec files of the whole-chip test hold `--rounds 2`, and `worker` in bwx12.c (lines 1654 and 1655) times one interval per round and position, so each kernel is timed in 2 intervals per process.

defects.before: Exit status: 0 all checks passed, 1 a check failed, 2 a file could not be used.
defects.after: Exit status: 0 all checks passed, 1 a check failed, 2 a file could not be used or the arguments are wrong.
defects.evidence: Lines 287 to 289 and 292 to 294 of the script return 2 for an option without a value, for more than 2 file arguments and for an unknown option.

defects.before: with the option `--stop common` of the whole-chip test it reads the clock in lines 1688 and 1700 and calls the kernel through `call` in line 1695.
defects.after: with the option `--stop common` of the whole-chip test it reads the start time of an interval in line 1688. It calls the kernel through `call` in line 1695 and reads the clock after each call in line 1700. The last of these clock reads is the end time of the interval.
defects.evidence: bwx12.c line 1688 is `t0 = now_ns()`, line 1700 is `t1 = now_ns()` inside the `do ... while (t1 < deadline)` loop after each `call`, line 1723 stores `r.t_end = t1`, and line 1681 holds a third clock read (the wait for the start) that the old sentence did not separate from the two reads that bound the interval.

defects.before: every thread runs a sequence of kernels, and each run of a kernel is one timed interval.
defects.after: every thread runs a sequence of kernels. In one timed interval a thread calls one kernel only, one or more times.
defects.evidence: In `worker` of bwx12.c the warm-up call of line 1669 is a run of the kernel outside every timed interval, and the timed interval between the clock reads of lines 1688 and 1700 holds one call per 2 MiB chunk (lines 1694 to 1701), so "each run of a kernel is one timed interval" is false when "run" is read as one call.

defects.before: The files `listing.txt` and `offsets.tsv` in the build folder have the recorded values (computed in this task). `go.sh` stops unless the binary has the recorded value [Ref5].
defects.after: The files `listing.txt` and `offsets.tsv` in the build folder have the recorded values (computed in this task). The binary `bwx12` is not in the local folders. So its sha256 value is known from the records only. `go.sh` stops unless the binary has the recorded value [Ref5].
